Nigeria’s First Lady, Oluremi Tinubu, has empowered over 5,000 women in Zamfara State, as her visit also marked the historic moment of the first First Lady’s official visit to the North-Western state. The empowerment was held at the APC North-West Women’s Mega Rally and Empowerment Programme, which she hosted in person at the Trade Fair Complex on Thursday in Gusau, the state capital. According to a statement made available to PUNCH Online on Monday, the First Lady was welcomed by thousands of residents and supporters at the venue. Ahead of the rally, the Co-Director, All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council Women Mobilisation Directorate, Betta Edu, and the other leaders of the directorate, on behalf of the First Lady, empowered women at a town hall stakeholders engagement meeting and supported businesses at the market with a humanitarian outreach for women and children at the hospitals. Tinubu said that the empowerment has been part of the Renewed Hope Initiative since its inception, adding that it was borne out of love for the people and not politically motivated. She was also conferred with the title of ‘Jagaban Matan Arewa’ by the Zamfara State Council of Chiefs. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources The event was led by Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal; his wife, Huriyya Lawal; former governors; First Ladies from the North-West; among others. “Before the rally, Senator Tinubu met with traditional rulers in the state to seek their blessings. She was subsequently conferred with the title of ‘Jagaban Matan Arewa’ by the Chairman of the Zamfara State Council of Chiefs and Emir of Anka, Alhaji Attahiru Muhammad Ahmad,” the statement partly read. She expressed her delight at visiting the state as she described her visit as a demonstration of solidarity and compassion, particularly towards women affected by insecurity, poverty and limited economic opportunities. “This is the happiest day of my life. Except for Zamfara, I have been in all 36 states of Nigeria, including the FCT. I have always wanted to come to Zamfara, and today I have fulfilled that,” she said. The statement continued, “She said the Renewed Hope Initiative had continued to empower women since its inception, insisting that its interventions went beyond political campaigns. “The only party that empowers during the campaign, and it is not about the campaign; we have been empowering from day one. And that is why it is not politics but love for our people.” The First Lady also conveyed President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to the state, assuring residents that the President would continue working for their benefit. She also commended the airport and other infrastructure built by the governor, saying, ” With this airport in place, I and my husband, the President, will come to Zamfara again and again.” Earlier, Lawal thanked the First Lady for her support through the Renewed Hope Initiative, particularly its food outreach programme. He described her visit as historic, saying her presence represented more than an official engagement. He said empowering women remained central to the state’s efforts to strengthen families, improve economic prosperity, and promote sustainable peace. The governor also declared the support of his administration and the people of Zamfara for the President’s re-election bid. “I assure Your Excellency that Zamfara’s government and people unwaveringly support Mr President’s second term. With the women here and the men supporting them, Zamfara and the North-West will deliver for Mr President come January 2027,” he said.
